newsitem.title: Australia: Long Australia bond yields hit 3-1/2 month lows.
newsitem.headline: Long Australia bond yields hit 3-1/2 month lows.

text.p: *Long-dated Australian bond yields struck their lowest level since mid-February as the market continued its recent bull run, although turnover was relatively light.
Long-dated Australian bond yields struck their lowest level since mid-February as the market continued its recent bull run, although turnover was relatively light, traders said.

"It's a very low volume day. There's still the expectation of a rate cut in the next few days, and it may be a spin-off from the turmoil in Europe," said Chris Bell, Director of Treasury at Dresdner Australia.
However, he added that no one really expected there to be a rate move so soon after the surprise May 23 easing, but the market was leaving nothing to chance.

The Reserve Bank held its monthly board meeting today and the market over the next few days will be monitoring the central bank's market operations at 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT), when rate changes are usually announced, on the off chance of a further easing. Official rates currently stand at 5.5 percent.

The market was also underpinned by a firm U.S. Treasury market in the face of Monday's jump in the May NAPM index, which gained support from a rise in the U.S. dollar against the mark after the unexpected Socialist win at last weekend's French elections.

Traders said there was no reaction to the Canadian election, although Australian/Canadian spreads had narrowed when the Canadian dollar had fallen amid fears that the Liberal party was going to lose it majority.
The Canadian dollar has since rallied on projections that the ruling Liberals will form another majority government.
The local market had got off to a slow start amid hedging of three domestic corporate issues for Macquarie Bank's securitisation arm PUMA, BTR Nylex and St George Bank, traders added.

The local market slightly outperformed the U.S., but eventually lost ground to Canada on projections that the Liberals would form a majority government. New Zealand bonds rallied as they played catch up to advance seen in dollar bloc bonds while their markets were closed on Monday.
